text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ten Opposition Members of Parliament ask Kenyans to reject alliance of opposition leaders Kenneth Matiba and Raila Odinga, saying it was only advancing the chances of the ruling KANU party to win the coming year's general election.

- Pressure mounts on Agriculture Minister Simeon Nyachae to quit his cabinet portfolio with Nandi branch (Rift Valley) leaders from the ruling party KANU supporting a weekend call by the chairman of Kenya Farmers Association that he resigns.
- President Daniel arap Moi directs police to crackdown on those with firearms after expiry of his amnesty deadline.

- Kenya Breweries Ltd chairman Jeremiah Kiereini says it will spend 1.0 billion shillings to set up a new bottling line with a capacity of 80,000 bottles per hour at the Ruaraka Tusker plant on edge of Nairobi.
- Opposition Democratic Party of Kenya chairman Mwai Kibaki endorsed as the sole opposition presidential candidate by his native Nyeri district of central Kenya.

- Opposition Ford-Kenya party factional leader Raila Odinga accuses Kisumu Rural Member of Parliament Professor Anyang Nyong'o of sabotaging his activities and regrets that the latter is set on forming another opposition party before the coming general election.
